node.title: Re: problem with regex
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [zerodmg],

See the discussion of m/PATTERN/ in [doc://perlop#Regexp-Quote-Like-Operators]: In scalar context, $string=~/.../ returns true/false for whether the match succeeded or not, in list context it returns the capture groups (unless you use the /g modifier, then the return value is different). The latter is what [tybalt89] is showing you in the [id://1177726|example], putting parens around the variable(s) in a my ($x) = ... assignment causes the right side to be evaluated in list context.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
